_provenance: vevov, created 2026-08-19 by copying tovez.json (stakeholder direction). Only identity/connection/vision carry vevov's own facts; EVERY calibration value below is tovez's, held as a placeholder pending operator-supplied numbers. Do not read a vevov measurement off this file until the section's own _provenance note is replaced. NOTE ALSO: as of this writing vevov is NOT running the firmware this config targets, so nothing here has been flashed to or read back from the robot.

connection._wifi_note: Empty on purpose -- the documented 'no WiFi module' state (wifi_setup.py treats a falsy wifi_ip as nothing to do). tovez's 192.168.4.11 was NOT copied, because two robots cannot hold one address. Fill in vevov's own if it gets a WiFi module.

vision._tag_note: Tag 53, assigned to vevov 2026-08-19 and registered with the AprilCam daemon the same day (owner=vevov, z=11.8cm), taking id 53 over from the previous owner=calibration registration. tag_offset_z=118.0 mm is OPERATOR-CONFIRMED. tag_offset_x/y are 0.0 = IDENTITY = UNMEASURED, not a measurement that came out zero: with identity offsets the camera reports the RAW TAG position, not vevov's centre of rotation, so any world_xy read for this robot is off by however far the tag sits from centre (tovez's is -41.0 mm). Measure with the three-reading in-place-rotation fit described in tovez.json's vision._tag_note, then update BOTH this block and the daemon registration. camera_distance_scale is tovez's value, not measured on vevov.

geometry._provenance: VEVOV-MEASURED 2026-08-28, after the stakeholder rebuilt the chassis (front caster removed, drive wheels moved forward, smaller wheels fitted). Artifact: pxt-nezha-diffdrive captures/vevov-wheel-scale-20260828.md. travel_calib: four camera-truthed raw legs (100/100/90/90 cm) gave scale 0.897-0.904 against the firmware's belief; anchored on the stakeholder's TAPE (90.4 cm for a commanded 100 cm) -> 0.7878*0.904 = 0.7122 mm/deg, implying an 81.6 mm wheel where the old bake assumed 90.3 mm. trackwidth 128.0 is the stakeholder's CALIPER measurement (geometric, never 'corrected'). rotational_slip 0.995: a four-size pivot sweep (40/70/100/130 mm, 16 pivots, |resid| <= 0.86 deg) fitted |d_theta| = 0.8055 deg/mm * d + 6.08 deg; dividing the slope by the 0.904 travel scale gives an effective track of 128.6 mm, which matches the 128.0 caliper to 0.5% -- so this chassis has essentially NO wheel scrub, and the ~0.80 the raw numbers implied was a 10% wheel error and a 12% track error stacking. NOTE the fit also carries a +6.08 deg FIXED per-pivot term that is NOT scrub and is deliberately not folded into rotational_slip (gopiv shows the same shape at +10.2 deg); folding it in would fit one pivot size and mis-turn every other.

firmware_bake._pivot_overrun_provenance: VEVOV-MEASURED 2026-08-29 (pxt-nezha-diffdrive captures/vevov-square-20260829/runC.json, runC2.json; reports/vevov-tour-C-firmware-and-telemetry-20260829.md S4): thirteen MOVE_X pivots of 3-90 deg on the playfield, firmware 0.20260829.1 (speed floor 70 mm/s), all landed a CONSTANT +1.3..+2.7 deg (mean ~2.0) past their command in the robot's OWN encoders, camera agreeing to ~1 deg -- +3.2 -> +5.1, -2.6 -> -4.4, +87.3 -> +89.2. Constant, not proportional, so it is a per-wheel end-of-move distance: 2 deg * (128 mm / 2) = 2.2 mm. Subtracted from every rotation target by MotionEngine::pivotOverrunMm_. Mechanism UNVERIFIED (one kernel tick at the 70 mm/s floor is 2.3 mm); re-measure if the speed floor changes.
firmware_bake._note: Opt-in: make_deploy.py's _inject_geometry() bakes exactly these into motion_engine.h in the per-robot scratch copy. Robots without this block keep the firmware defaults, which is why adding it here does not touch tovez/gopiv/togov/zetuv.
firmware_bake._provenance: REGRESSION-DERIVED 2026-08-28 (supersedes the same day's earlier single-leg values travel_calib 0.7122, rotational_slip 0.995). Artifacts: pxt-nezha-diffdrive captures/regressions-20260828/ and docs/vevov-regressions-20260828.md. DISTANCE: 39 trials, 10-200 cm every 5 cm, 67 straight legs, camera-truthed -> measured = 0.98379*commanded - 0.097 cm, i.e. PURE SCALE -1.62% with a 1 mm intercept across a 20x range, so there is no per-move overshoot term. travel_calib 0.7122 * 0.98379 = 0.70066. TURN: 89 turns, 10-720 deg both directions -> camera error -2.426%/deg +1.49 (CCW), +2.355%/deg -1.63 (CW); antisymmetric to 3%, so drivetrain rather than a world-frame bias. COUPLING, and the reason rotational_slip is NOT set to the full -2.43%: rotation is driven by wheel ARC, which scales with travel_calib, so the -1.62% common part belongs to travel_calib and only the -0.81% residual is rotation-only scrub. rotational_slip 0.995/1.0081 = 0.987. motion_engine.h warns explicitly against correcting this twice. NOT folded in: a fixed per-turn overshoot the encoder also sees (+2.0 deg mean below 90 deg, +0.6 deg above 200) -- it does not scale with angle, so baking it into a scale constant would fit one turn size and mis-turn every other. The camera error crosses zero near 125 deg, which is why 30/90/720 deg spot checks previously disagreed: all three were correct.

geometry._otos_note: OTOS reads 4.54% SHORT of camera truth over the same distance sweep (0.95462*commanded + 0.563 cm) and the error GROWS with distance (~2.5% at 10 cm to ~4.4% at 200 cm), so it is NOT a linear-scalar miscalibration. UNEXPLAINED and deliberately NOT corrected here -- do not use the OTOS for absolute distance until this is understood. Its lever arm IS measured and applied (see armX/armY in test.ts).

motors._vel_gains_domain: duty [-1,1] (NezhaMotor MotorVelocityPid); NOT the old PWM-percent scale
motors._provenance: VEVOV-MEASURED 2026-08-19 (pxt-nezha-diffdrive bench session): fwd signs from stakeholder-observed reversed drive under tovez defaults (left port2 +1, right port1 -1 in the pxt extension's convention: sign multiplies both commanded duty and encoder). travel_calib from a commanded-80cm run: odometry 798 mm vs tape 825 mm -> 0.7837*825/798 = 0.8102, combined-wheel value written to both sides (per-wheel split unmeasured). Confirming run after bake: odometry 798 mm vs tape 795 mm (0.38%). Velocity-PID gains below remain tovez placeholders (different firmware; not used by the pxt extension).
